text:
sam: main is red after the merge — compatibility-check job failed on the runtime assertions. link: https://ci.redwood.example/runs/98765 :eyes:
ci-bot: build 98765 · pipeline failed · job: compatibility-check · stage: integration · failed 3m ago
henry: that was my merge (PR #1423). I ran the unit tests locally and they passed. pinging for a quick triage.
maria: can someone paste the failing log lines? I can't access the runner UI from mobile. :phone:
devops: I'm on it, re-running the failing job now (manual retrigger). If it passes we can close the noisy alert, if not we'll need a bisect.
ci-bot: rerun requested by devops · rerun id: 98765.2
ci-bot: rerun finished · compatibility-check FAILED · new run 98765.2 · elapsed 02:14
pri: quick look — error seems to be an assert in tokenizer mapping during compatibility matrix setup. copying the tail log:
```
AssertionError: mismatch in tokenizer vocab mapping
Expected shape (50265,) got (50266,)
  File "/srv/runtime/tests/compat_matrix.py", line 128, in setup_tokenizer
    assert token_map.shape == expected
```
maria: interesting — shape off by one. could be a generated token added in the last commit. henry, did your PR touch tokenizer files or vocab generation?
henry: I changed the invocation of the build pipeline but not the vocab. PR diff: no_vocab_changes.txt — but my PR bumped the submodule commit for the tokenizers package (tokenizers@c03f2).
sam: okay, two paths: (A) bisect to find exact commit that introduced the extra token in tokenizers package, or (B) hotfix tests to relax the strict assert while we investigate. I'm leaning to bisect first. Who can pick this up as first responder? :raised_hand:
henry: I can start a bisect of tokenizers submodule range (c00000..c03f2) — but I'm on a call for 30m. If someone can kick it off, I'll continue after.
pri: I can start the bisect now. I'll run `tools/submodule-bisect --repo tokenizers --range c00000..c03f2 --test "python -m pytest tests/compat_matrix.py::test_tokenizer_setup"` and report back with the first bad commit.
ci-bot: job queued: bisect-12345 started by pri
pri: first bisect result looks like commit c019a introduced an extra vocab entry — linking commit: https://git.example/tokenizers/commit/c019a. It adds an extra token for legacy emoji handling.
maria: that matches. we should decide whether to treat that token as intended (update expected shape) or constrain tokenizer build to match previous behavior.
sam: given this was a submodule bump included in henry's merge, we should revert the bump for the immediate rollback to unbreak main, then open a follow-up to either accept the tokenizer change or update tests. henry, can you open the revert?
henry: yes, I'll push a revert of the submodule pin and trigger a hotfix merge.
devops: noted — once revert merge lands I'll trigger a single-job pipeline to confirm compatibility-check passes before we close the page.
pri: +1 on the revert for fast restore. created issue to track long-term decision: https://issues.redwood.example/RED-924
henry: revert PR opened: #1430 · merging now.
ci-bot: merge detected for PR #1430 · starting post-merge pipeline (run 98766)
ci-bot: pipeline 98766 · compatibility-check · PASSED · 01:47
sam: good recovery — main is green again. thanks everyone for the quick bisect and revert. :tada:
maria: great teamwork. leaving a note in the incident log (incidents/internal) with the root cause and follow-up steps.
henry: will follow up with a postmortem comment in PR #1423 explaining the submodule risk and better checklist for future bumps.
pri: added the commit c019a to the regression tests so we catch this matrix drift earlier.
sam: closing thread — if anything flares up, re-open here. :white_check_mark:
